# Part-Time Barista

**[Café Name]** | [City, State] | Part-time, 15–25 hours/week | $[X]–$[Y]/hour + tips

## About Us
[Café Name] is a neighborhood coffee shop serving carefully sourced espresso, seasonal drinks, and fresh pastries. We're a friendly, fast-moving team that cares about great coffee and making every customer feel welcome.

## What You'll Do
- Prepare espresso drinks, brewed coffee, tea, and other beverages to our recipes and quality standards
- Greet customers, take orders, and handle cash and card payments
- Keep the bar, dining area, and restrooms clean and stocked
- Open or close the shop following our checklists
- Help with inventory, deliveries, and restocking
- Share your ideas for new drinks and ways to improve the shop

## What We're Looking For
- Positive, friendly attitude and a willingness to learn
- Ability to stay calm and efficient during busy rushes
- Reliability and good communication with teammates
- Able to stand for long periods and lift up to 25 lbs
- Availability for some weekends and early mornings or evenings
- Barista or food-service experience is a plus, but not required. We'll train you.

## What We Offer
- Competitive hourly pay plus shared tips
- Flexible, predictable scheduling
- Free drinks during shifts and a discount on beans and food
- Paid training with hands-on espresso coaching
- A supportive team and room to grow, including opportunities to become a shift lead

## How to Apply
Send a short resume, or a few lines about yourself, to **[email address]**. You can also drop by **[address]** and ask for **[Manager Name]**. Please include your availability.

*[Café Name] is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and will provide reasonable accommodations on request.*

---
Fill in the bracketed fields. If you tell me the café's name, location, pay, and vibe, I can tailor the post, or make a shorter version for social media or job boards.

# Part-Time Barista — [Café Name], [Neighborhood/City]

**Pay:** $[X]–$[Y]/hour + 100% of tips (tips average ~$[Z]/hr, so total earnings run about $[X+Z]–$[Y+Z]/hr)
**Hours:** 12–24 hrs/week. Shifts are 4–8 hours, including weekday mornings, weekends, or both.
**Start date:** [Date]. Paid training is included.

---

## About us

[Café Name] is a [number]-seat neighborhood café that roasts [or: sources] its coffee from [Roaster]. We serve about [N] drinks a day. Most of our customers are regulars, and we know many of them by name and by order. We want our baristas to be good at the craft, calm during a rush, and glad to see whoever walks in.

## The role

You'll work the espresso bar, the register, and the pastry case. A typical shift includes:

- Pulling and dialing in espresso, steaming milk, and making drinks to our recipes and standards
- Taking orders, handling payments, and answering questions about the menu
- Opening or closing: setting up, restocking, cleaning equipment, and counting the drawer
- Keeping the bar, the floor, and the restrooms clean and stocked
- Following food-safety and allergen procedures every time

## What you'll get

- **Real training.** You'll get a 2-week paid ramp-up with a trainer. It covers espresso, milk texturing, tasting, and workflow. You do not need to know latte art on day one.
- **Predictable scheduling.** Schedules are posted [2] weeks ahead. You can list your availability and we'll honor it. Shift swaps are easy.
- **Free drinks on shift** and a [30%] discount, plus a free bag of beans each month.
- **Skills that last.** We'll pay for a barista skills course or a tasting workshop after [90 days]. Paths to lead barista and trainer roles are open to part-timers.
- **Tips shared fairly:** [describe, e.g., pooled and split by hours worked, paid weekly].
- [Optional: Paid sick leave as required by law, a meal during longer shifts, transit subsidy.]

## Who we're looking for

**Must have**
- Availability for at least [two weekend shifts or three weekday mornings] per week
- Comfort being on your feet for a full shift and lifting up to [25–30] lbs
- Friendliness under pressure. You can stay warm with a line out the door.
- Reliability. You show up on time and you tell us early if something changes.
- Eligibility to work in [country]. You must be [18+ / of legal working age]. [Food handler card, or willingness to get one within 30 days, at our cost.]

**Nice to have (not required)**
- Prior café, restaurant, or customer-service experience
- Curiosity about coffee. Tell us the best cup you've ever had.
- Bilingual in [language]
- Experience with [POS system]

If you're a student, a creative, or have another job and want steady hours, you'd fit in well here. Many of our baristas do.

## Our approach to hiring

We hire for attitude and teach the rest. If you don't match every bullet above, apply anyway. We're an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background, and we'll make reasonable accommodations at any stage of hiring. Just let us know what you need.

## How to apply

1. Send a short note to **[email]** or apply at **[link]**. Include your availability and a line or two on why you'd like to work here. A resume is welcome but optional.
2. We'll reply within [3] business days.
3. Come in for a 30-minute chat and a paid 1-hour working trial on the bar. We'll make you a drink, and you can make us one.
4. We'll make a decision within [48 hours] of your trial.

*Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. We plan to fill this role by [date].*

---

### Notes for the hiring manager (delete before posting)

- **Fill in the pay range.** Posts with a stated wage get more and better applicants, and many jurisdictions now require it (e.g., CO, NY, CA, WA, IL).
- **Be honest about hours.** Part-time candidates mainly want to know which shifts are needed. If the real need is weekends, say so up front to avoid mismatches.
- **Keep the tips line only if it's accurate.** Use a trailing 3-month average.
- **Check local rules** on tip pooling, scheduling notice, and minimum age.
- **Shorter versions:** For Indeed or a window flyer, use the header, pay, hours, three bullets from "The role," the top three perks, and the apply line. I can draft those if you'd like.
- **Interview questions I'd use:** "Tell me about a time you dealt with a frustrated customer." "How do you stay organized when four things need doing at once?" "What would you want to learn here in your first three months?"

I can tailor this to your actual café, with its name, pay, location, and voice, whether that's playful, minimalist, or specialty-coffee serious. Send me the details and I'll produce the final version.

# Part-Time Barista, [Shop Name], [Neighborhood]

**We're looking for a friendly, reliable part-time barista to join our small team and help make [Neighborhood]'s mornings better.**

## What you'll do day to day
- Open or close the shop: setting up, restocking, and locking up at the end of the shift
- Make espresso and milk drinks (lattes, flat whites, cappuccinos) and filter coffee, to a consistent standard
- Take orders and payments at the till
- Keep the counter, machines, and seating area clean and tidy
- Greet regulars by name (eventually) and make newcomers feel welcome

## What you need
- **No experience required.** If you're keen and willing to learn, we'll train you on the job.
- Availability on **weekend mornings**
- Reliability: turning up on time, every shift, matters more to us than anything on a CV
- A calm, friendly manner when it gets busy

## What we offer
- About **16-20 hours a week**
- **[$X-$Y] per hour, plus tips**
- Free staff drinks on shift
- Proper training in espresso, milk texturing, and running the shop

## This suits you if
You like being on your feet, enjoy chatting with people, can be counted on for early weekend starts, and want to learn real coffee skills. It probably isn't for you if you can't do weekend mornings or you'd rather work behind the scenes away from customers.

## How to apply
Send a short message to [email/contact method] with your name and answers to these two questions:

1. Are you able to work weekend mornings regularly? Please tell us which days and times you could do.
2. Do you have any customer-service experience (paid, voluntary, or informal)? A sentence or two is plenty. If not, just say so.

We'll aim to reply within [X days]. [Shop Name] is an equal opportunity employer.

---

## Placeholders to fill in
- **[Shop Name]** and **[Neighborhood]**
- **[$X-$Y]**: the hourly pay range
- **[email/contact method]**: where applications go
- **[X days]**: your reply timeframe
- Equal-opportunity line: keep, change, or remove to match your local requirements

**Assumed, not confirmed:** the 16-20 hours a week, the duties listed (including opening and closing, and the drink range), weekend-morning availability being required, and tips and staff drinks being part of the package.

## The one thing that would sharpen it most
The shop's **actual rota and pay rate**. Concrete shift times (for example, "Sat and Sun 7am-1pm plus one weekday") and a real pay figure will draw better-matched applicants than "about 16-20 hours" and a placeholder range.

## Before you post
- Have a **current barista confirm the duties and hours** match how the shop really runs.
- **Check the pay line** against local pay-transparency and minimum-wage rules. Some places require a stated range, and tips can't usually count toward meeting the minimum wage.
